suggestions.assertion: Skim test: reading only the first sentence of each paragraph ...
suggestions.reason: This was the only assertion to catch a real defect, and it is judged by eye. The teaser pattern that failed here ('Two principles drive the design.') is the exact shape writing.md names, so a first-sentence grep for '^(Two|Three|Several|A few) \w+ ' would make it mechanical and consistent across runs.

suggestions.assertion: invariants.md has at least two `### INV-NNN:` items and one of them captures ...
suggestions.reason: The wording 'one of them' penalizes the arguably better output of splitting source-of-truth and append-only into two invariants, as this run did. Reword to 'the items together capture'.

suggestions.assertion: No generated file still contains a template placeholder ...
suggestions.reason: check_run.py's regex requires an uppercase first letter, so a lowercase leftover like <project name> would pass silently. Here <repo-root> was fine because the template uses it as a literal, but the checker would not distinguish.

No assertion covers what the executor did best: it ran the code and surfaced a real code-vs-spec conflict (traceback on unknown priority) as a TODO instead of enshrining the bug or silently fixing it. An assertion like 'any behavior the executor found inconsistent is marked as a conflict, not specced as intended' would reward that and catch runs that paper over it.
Nothing checks that the commands AGENTS.md tells a newcomer to run actually work (python3 -m ticketdesk.cli ...). They do here, but a wrong invocation would pass every assertion.

eval_feedback.overall: Mechanical assertions are discriminating and all pass via check_run.py. The judgment assertions did their job once (skim test). The eval under-rewards conflict surfacing and over-specifies invariant decomposition.
